input.rationale: Section 13.5 gives us ownership of the interface code we create, but then hands ownership of those same Developments to Commerce One whenever it supports them on an ongoing basis — an effective assignment of our IP to the Vendor, which is walk-away territory. We delete the reversion; Commerce One's pre-existing IP and the Software itself remain untouched. We also note the agreement has no Customer Data ownership provision.

input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The hosting licence is perpetual and irrevocable, transferable to a successor via Section 14.1, permits unlimited sublicensing to our Customers, and Section 14.8 expressly allows us to subcontract portions of the Corio Services — so contractors and successors are covered and the walk-away risks (revocable at will, no path for third parties) are absent. Affiliates are not expressly named, which we note rather than flag.
